# Attribution and inherited terms

The submitted `K216_Partial_Selector_2026-10-20.zip` arrived in ProveIt commit `6ec69081ca2a4abc03c35b573e22eb0d939a6324`. Preserve its exact [original attribution](provenance/ATTRIBUTION.md). The new contribution is the partial-selector source and contextual allocation repair, the 164/183 marker quotient, exact 216-state presentations, deterministic reconstruction, 216-specific audits and article, prepared in collaboration with Vladimir Reshetnikov for ProveIt.

Preserve its [notice](provenance/k217-NOTICE.md) and original attribution alongside the existing inherited license directory. That parent retains Source149's dominated theorem, native-calculus/compiler ancestry, and earlier licenses. The joint-fold checker and symbolic runtime are inherited infrastructure, not216-specific inventions.

`opening_encoder` authored this exposition and independent static/saved-record reviews; `review_upstream_reflection` independently reviewed the ordinary calibration and new source-facing proof; root selects and runs the fresh checks and performs final publication. Those review/packaging roles do not transfer authorship of the submitted construction. Prior bounded helper searches by opening_encoder are separately attributed and were not exhaustive over this new reparse family.

Existing third-party terms remain those supplied by their original authors. This exposition does not relicense inherited code. Full original reports and embedded predecessors remain recoverable through [intake195](../../../../../SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/set-theory/zfc-closure-kernels/intake-195-reproduction.md).

# Attribution and inherited terms

The submitted K217 construction is Source152, `K217_Dominated_Continuation_2026-10-20.zip`, received at `8a1796545e`. Its original attribution is preserved unchanged in [provenance/ATTRIBUTION.md](provenance/ATTRIBUTION.md). Its new contribution is the three source reassociations, the exposed continuation selector, deletion of native state 400, exact tables and submitted verification packet.

The immediate predecessor is Source149's dominated-rho8 K218. Its notice is preserved unchanged as [provenance/parent-NOTICE.md](provenance/parent-NOTICE.md). It contributes the numerical domination theorem, finite recovery certificate and smaller common-input source. Its native-calculus, proof compiler, runtime and ZFC consistency ancestors are credited there and in the exact inherited notices below.

The complete parent `licenses/` directory is retained unchanged here, including ProveIt and Wade license texts, original and normalized-source notices, and source pins. The parent's `k219_LICENSE` and `k219_NOTICE-parent220.md` are retained in `provenance/`. Existing third-party terms remain those supplied by their original authors; this exposition does not relicense them. The new217 submission asserts no replacement license for inherited work.

`drop_contract` authored this candidate README/proof exposition and performed a second ordinary mathematical/source review. `review_upstream_reflection` independently reviewed the submitted proof and code closure. Root selected, ran and retained the fresh checks. `opening_encoder` independently reconstructed an isomorphic machine, preserved separately as corroboration. These review and packaging roles are distinct from authorship of the submitted construction and its predecessors.

The original report, main proof inputs, nested archive and full supplied provenance remain recoverable through the [intake192 instructions](../../../../../SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/set-theory/zfc-closure-kernels/intake-192-reproduction.md); they are not duplicated in this candidate directory.

# Attribution and reuse

Prepared on 20 October 2026 for Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt repository,
with ChatGPT-assisted research, implementation, and independent parallel
review. The new contribution is the dominated numerical-axiom recovery,
its finite proof certificate, the revised common-input enumeration
schedule, the 218-state literal construction, verification scripts,
research alternatives, and accompanying report.

The numerical calculus, seed bundle, ZFC consistency comparison,
all-natural macro library, and symbolic runtime induction engine build on
the pinned ProveIt K219 construction and its predecessors. The retained
notices credit Elliot Glazer, Mira, Jeff's busy-beaver development, Andrew
James Wade, BusyCoq, the Coq Library of Undecidability, and ProveIt's
accumulated reductions. Those contributions are not claimed as new here.

The inherited license and notices are retained in licenses/ and
provenance/. New material is supplied under the same MIT No Attribution
terms as the predecessor contribution. Existing third-party files retain
their own terms; this notice does not relicense them.

The full logical certificate is checked without invoking the proof-search
software that discovered it. Saved Prover9 input/output is included for
provenance; Prover9's implementation is not distributed in this archive.

The ordinary mathematical proof is formalizable in ZFC. A newly compiled
exact-K218 proof-assistant endpoint and an internal PA proof-code theorem
are not claimed.

# Provenance and attribution

New packet contribution: the context-correct partial-selector source, exact216-state tables, deterministic reconstruction and source/marker/blank validation, integrated full symbolic runtime evidence, and explanatory article, prepared in collaboration with Vladimir Reshetnikov for ProveIt.

The parent is the unmodified `K217_Dominated_Continuation_2026-10-20.zip` from ProveIt commit `8a1796545e33bf0c4bb52b6c92a6ced17362ca66`, SHA256 `4aa33f0c4844043d243fb7d01ef316d4b72de641864e5317525f7cfac7f5c809`. It retains the exact dominated-rho8 K218 archive, SHA256 `080b4fe855c109ab77588c01c9e012d9572afa7721682306370ccb2eb22cbea9`, including all notices and licenses, proof-search and theory ancestry, runtime/compiler sources, source calibration and previous articles.

`code/check_joint_fold.py` is copied byte-for-byte from the pinned K217 packet. `code/validate_native.py`, `code/runtime/symbolic_runtime.py`, `code/runtime/independent_runtime.py`, and `code/inputs/legacy_mapping.json` are copied byte-for-byte from the nested pinned K218 packet. They are inherited infrastructure, not newly claimed216-specific inventions. The source-CFG checker and216-specific construction/audit scripts accompany this new construction. No license is asserted here over inherited work; consult the intact notices and licenses within the included parent archives for their scopes.

The ancestry credits Mira and Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt project, Jeff's Rocq busy-beaver reference, Elliot Glazer's compact theory K/K230 development, and Andrew James Wade's Turing Machine Explorer compiler ancestry. See the original included attribution files for the detailed relationships.

# Attribution and scope

This new research contribution was prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt project. The new work consists of the 202-subtree command-specific input construction, the native state-81 helper-path reuse, the two successful command permutations, the exact 216-state tables, their independent audits and reproducible packet, and the new report sections that describe and prove those changes.

The dominated-rho8 theorem, propositional certificate, numerical calculus, proof-search architecture, arithmetic macro contracts, source language, and symbolic runtime infrastructure are inherited work. In particular, the dominated-row theorem reproduced in the report appendix is copied verbatim from the predecessor and is not claimed as a new contribution here.

The immediate predecessor is the unchanged `K217_Dominated_Continuation_2026-10-20.zip`, taken from ProveIt commit `8a1796545e33bf0c4bb52b6c92a6ced17362ca66`. It is retained under `parent/` and contains the unchanged `K218_Dominated_Rho8_2026-10-20.zip`. Their exact SHA-256 hashes are recorded in `inputs.json`. The predecessor's original attribution is reproduced in `PREDECESSOR_ATTRIBUTION.md`; the K218 notice is reproduced in `K218_NOTICE.md`. All embedded notices and licenses are retained.

The predecessor credits the architecture and machine work to Mira and the ProveIt project, the Rocq reference to Jeff's busy-beaver project, the compact theory K and K230 work to Elliot Glazer, and compiler ancestry to Andrew James Wade's Turing Machine Explorer. It also records BusyCoq and the Coq Library of Undecidability among the proof/calculus ancestry. Those original notices specify the exact scope of each contribution.

`code/build_dominated_source.py` and `sections/inherited_dominated_core.tex` are copied unchanged from K218. `source/baseline219.json` is the unchanged source input carried by that archive. `code/build_sources.py` and `code/audit_command_permutation.py` use the inherited structured-control/address-counter verification method, with new reconstruction, permutation, and selector/return-wrapper checks. The runtime checker is executed from the pinned nested archive rather than silently copied or modified. The independent source audit imports the unchanged `source_language.py` from the immediate predecessor.

The allocation witnesses document how the tables were found. Reproduction and certification use deterministic row recipes and the exact literal table; users need not trust or rerun a numerical optimizer.

New material is provided under the same MIT No Attribution terms as the ProveIt predecessor; see `licenses/LICENSE.ProveIt`. This does not relicense inherited third-party components, whose original licenses and notices remain authoritative.

There is no newly compiled exact-K216 Lean/Rocq endpoint, internally checked PA theorem, absolute consistency proof, state-minimality theorem, or universal discovery-priority claim. Independent parallel review denotes separately implemented checks and mathematical review within this collaboration, not an external human endorsement or independent authorship claim.
